claim_traces.claim_title: Humans only use 10% of their brains
claim_traces.claim_text: "Humans only use 10% of their brain capacity — the other 90% remains dormant and untapped."
reasoning_steps: The claim that humans only use 10% of their brain capacity is a widely debunked neuroscientific myth

Modern neuroimaging technologies, such as functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) and positron emission tomography (PET), demonstrate that virtually all parts of the brain are active and utilized, even during sleep or simple tasks

Additionally, evolutionary biology and clinical neurology show that unutilized brain tissue would atrophy, and even minor damage to nearly any area of the brain results in profound cognitive or physical deficits, disproving the notion of a 90% dormant reserve.
